I could be wrong, but I suspect that this is a mac/R problem, not a
statnet problem.  A similar thing happened to me when I upgraded from R
2.3.x to 2.5.0 on my (non-intel) mac.  It resulted in my inability to
build ANY package from source because; the problem was not limited to
statnet.

I corrected the problem, if you can call it corrected, by reinstalling R
2.3.  If anyone has any advice about how to deal with this without having
to install an older version, I'd love to hear it (and I hope folks don't
mind a non-statnet-related post in this case).  I remember that Mark
Handcock told me he did not have this issue with his (intel) mac, so I'm
puzzled.

Dave Hunter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Re: StatNet on Mac
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,

I've come across this issue before with an earlier version of StatNet  
and R.  I have a crude workaround, in which I edit the line in the  
file "statnet.so" to correct the path to the shared library for the  
current version of R.

i.e. from:
�/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.4/Resources/lib/ 
libR.dylib������ ���

to:
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.5/Resources/lib/ 
libR.dylib������ ���

It seems to work.  I've also tried creating a folder in the directory  
"/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.4/Resources/" called  
"lib" and copied the shared library "libR.dylib" into it, and that  
seemed to work also.

Best,
- Art.

messages.subject: [statnet_help] StatNet Help
messages.body_plain:
If I am not mistaken, this is a gcc problem.  The latest Apple developer 
tools apparently lack a Fortran compiler. Here is some text from the
JAGS 0.90 manual (http://www-fis.iarc.fr/~martyn/software/jags/manual.pdf):


> A.2.4 Mac OS X: instructions from Bill Northcott If trying to build
> software on Mac OS X you really need to use Tiger (10.4.x) or Panther
>  (10.3.x). The open source support has improved greatly in recent
> releases. You also need the latest version of Apple?s Xcode
> development tools. These are available as a free download from 
> http://developer.apple.com. You need to set up a free login to ADC.
> The Apple developer tools do not include a Fortran compiler. Without
> Fortran, you will not be able to build libRmath. The GNU g77 Fortran
> compiler is included in the R binary distribution available on CRAN.
> Install the R binary and select ?GNU Fortran?, and ?Tcl/Tk? from
> the optional components in the customize step of the installer. 
> IMPORTANT for Tiger (10.4.x) users: The default C/C++ compiler for
> Tiger is gcc-4. This is not compatible with g77. Before trying to
> build anything using g77, the default compiler must be changed with
> the command sudo gcc_select 3.3. (It won?t hurt to do this on Panther
>  as well.) gcc-4 uses a new Fortran compiler known as gfortran. This
> should be usable in the near future, but for the moment some hacking
> would be required.

I don't know if this is still true but it would explain why you can't 
load statnet.so, and you are using gcc 4.0...

I am going to go in and try to build on my office machine later today 
and will let you know if these various suggestions solve the problem.

Cheers,

Jamie

messages.subject: [statnet_help] nested homophily terms
messages.body_plain:
greetings,

i have a somewhat detailed question regarding homophily statistics that 
i am hoping one of the experts can help me with! i apologize for the 
length- i will try to be as specific as possible to avoid confusion.

i have a large (n=1640), directed social network that i am trying to 
model, and i have a number of attributes to work with. my problem 
concerns two of these attributes in particular- 'race' and 'ethnicity.' 
these are not traditional race and ethnicity attributes, because 
ethnicity is actually completely NESTED within race. more specifically, 
i have 6 categories for the attribute of race: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. i also 
have 12 categories for the attribute of ethnicity: 10, 11, 20, 21, 31, 
32, 33, 34, 40, 50, 51, and 60. the two attributes are related in that 
ethnicity 10 and 11, combined, form race 1; ethnicity 20 and 21, 
combined, form race 2... and so on. ethnicity, then, is completed nested 
in race- two people with the same ethnicity, by definition, MUST have 
the same race. race 4 and 6 cannot be further divided, and so race 4 is 
identical to ethnicity 40, and race 6 is identical to ethnicity 60.

our aim is essentially to understand the respective roles of racial and 
ethnic homophily in our social network- CONTROLLING for the role of the 
other. in other words, some ethnic groups may care only about ethnicity 
in forming ties, but not about race; while other groups may care only 
about race, and not ethnicity.

question 1: is it possible to model these (nested) attributes in the 
first place? discerning the role of ethnic homophily while controlling 
for racial homophily, and vice versa? i have talked to several people 
about this issue. on one hand, some have told me that i must leave out a 
'reference group' for each in order for the model to work. on the other 
hand, others have told me it is ok to just go ahead and throw both 
attributes into the model- and my preliminary results seem to confirm 
that this is in fact works just fine, and i get intelligible results 
(see 'model 1', attached).

question 2: assuming that i am doing this right- i.e. that model 1 is 
ok- i run into another problem further down the line. you'll note that 
in model 1, statnet appropriately dropped the homophily terms for 
ethnicity 40 and 60- because, as mentioned above, these categories are 
duplicates of race 4 and race 6, respectively. however, something seems 
to go wrong when i switch over to a dyad-dependence model. when i add a 
"mutual" term for reciprocal ties, three bad things happen (see 'model 
2', attached). first, i do not receive MCMC s.e. statistics (i assume i 
should be receiving these because i am now in dyad-dependence land, 
which is no longer equivalent to pseudo-likelihood estimation). second, 
some of my p-values shoot way up such that fewer terms are significant. 
and third, the homophily terms for ethnicity 40 and 60 are now 
maintained, when they should be dropped. what am i doing wrong here? i 
wonder if problems 1 and 2 are the result of problem 3, because the 
model is keeping terms it shouldn't be keeping. if this is so, how do i 
get statnet to drop these duplicate terms again?

if there is anything that i can clarify, please let me know. thank you 
in advance for your help! i have been beating my head against the wall 
for some time with this issue, and hopefully can finally resolve it and 
get on my way.

kevin lewis
kmlewis@fas.harvard.edu
